mcpSupport: MCP can read this help and inspect script effects on traffic it has access to. It cannot read or edit script source, test scripts, or enable them. Use Automation → Scripts for those actions.

sections.title: Write and enable a script
paragraphs: Use scripts for conditional changes, JSON transformations, local responses, or logic shared between a request and its response. Rules handle fixed header and text replacements.
Save draft keeps your work. Save & enable applies it to new requests; Save & apply updates an enabled script. Unsaved edits and failed builds leave the applied script unchanged.

Pause script stops selecting new requests. Requests already in progress finish with the version they started with. Scripts run on traffic received by the proxy; direct Composer sends and imported captures do not run scripts.
Export synchronous handlers and import helpers and types from transmog:api. Browser and Node APIs, network access, files, and timers are unavailable. Handlers cannot return promises.
If the applied script becomes unavailable, matching requests can fail. Choose Retry applied script, apply a fix, or Pause script.

sections.title: Callbacks, decisions and permissions
paragraphs: Every callback receives the request, parameters, state, and context. The table shows its additional inputs and allowed decisions. These inputs are read-only.

Return a result with a decision: continue, edit, respond, or abort. Helpers such as pass(), edit(), and respondJson() build the result. Combine related header, status, and body changes in one edit. Empty bytes clear a body.

Enable the capabilities your changes need. List edited header names in Writable headers; Transmog manages Host, Content-Length, Content-Encoding, Transfer-Encoding, and connection headers. Sensitive values are hidden unless Read sensitive headers is enabled. Header helpers throw when a requested value is hidden.

Method and URL changes need Rewrite request method and URL. A different origin also needs Allow cross-origin URL changes. URLs must be absolute HTTP(S), without credentials or fragments. Status changes need Change response status and accept 200–599. Local responses need Return responses or select assets; abort needs Abort requests.
Errors or unpermitted changes in request/response callbacks fail the request. onCompleted and onFailed only report findings; their errors become diagnostics.

phases.decisions: Continue; edit headers, method or URL; inline response; named response asset; abort

sections.title: Filters, buffering and limits
paragraphs: Host and method filters match exactly, ignoring case. The path-prefix filter is case-sensitive. Blank filters match all. Filters select a script before onRequestHead; source conditions do not change them, and URL rewrites do not remove later callbacks.

Body callbacks need Read bounded bodies; changing or clearing a body also needs Replace bodies. Set request body media types and response body media types/statuses to limit which messages are buffered. Blank lists match all. Local response bodies are excluded unless you include them.
Body callbacks receive complete, decoded bytes. Matching messages wait in memory before headers are forwarded, even when the callback returns pass(). Avoid unending streams such as SSE.
Default body limits are 1 MiB for input and output. Callbacks have 100 ms to run, with 64 MiB of JavaScript heap. Exceeding a limit fails the request.

sections.title: Parameters and request state
paragraphs: Declare text, boolean, or integer parameters in Filters, capabilities, and parameters; read them through event.parameters. They are saved with the script, so do not use them for secrets.
Use event.state to carry this script’s JSON values between callbacks for one request. Returning state replaces it; omitting state keeps it. Module globals are shared across requests.
Use context.elapsedMs for durations and context.nowUnixMs for timestamps. context.source is proxy for proxy traffic and sandbox for tests.

sections.title: Use API helpers
paragraphs: Import helpers by name, for example import { utf8Decode } from "transmog:api". For completion, use import * as api from "transmog:api" and type api. Open Full transmog:api namespace for signatures and types.

pass() leaves traffic unchanged; edit() changes a message. setHeader, appendHeader, and removeHeader build header operations. headerText and headerValues return all matching values, including duplicates. requestUrl and the query helpers work with URLs and query pairs.
utf8Encode/utf8Decode convert between text and bytes. UTF-8 decoding rejects invalid bytes by default. base64Encode/base64Decode convert bytes and padded Base64.

readText and readJson read UTF-8 bodies. replaceText, replaceJson, and replaceForm update the body and Content-Type together: enable Replace bodies and allow content-type in Writable headers. readForm/replaceForm support URL-encoded forms, including repeated fields; they do not support multipart forms.
Cookie helpers preserve repeated Cookie pairs and separate Set-Cookie fields. Cookie values are not URL-decoded. Use null for flag attributes such as Secure.
respondText and respondJson return a local response. respondAsset("id@revision") selects an available saved response at onRequestHead only.

sections.title: Logs, annotations and failures
paragraphs: Use console.log, debug, info, warn, error, or trace to inspect execution. Log individual fields: objects appear as labels rather than expanded values.
Open Developer details in test results or Script findings for logs, exceptions, and call frames. Selecting a frame shows the code that ran, preserving your draft.

Annotations add notes to saved traffic and need Add saved traffic annotations. Diagnostics and console output are temporary and are not saved with traffic. Avoid logging credentials or other sensitive content.
onFailed receives event.failure, one of the categories below, without the underlying error message.

examples.title: Log a callback without changing its decision
examples.settings: No extra capabilities. Console output is temporary.

sections.title: Debug a script
paragraphs: Set breakpoints in the editor gutter, then choose Debug test. It runs the current test input without enabling the script. Use Debugger options to choose when to pause on exceptions.
When paused, inspect the call stack and local variables. Inspection is read-only; expressions and getters are not evaluated. Draft edits take effect on Restart.

Use F8 to continue, F10 to step over, F11 to step into, and Shift+F11 to step out. Return to editor or Escape hides the debugger; Stop ends the run. Pauses expire after 60 seconds and sessions after 10 minutes.

Debug next matching exchange uses the applied script on real traffic. Review its version and filters, then arm it. Other requests using that script may fail while it is reserved, and client/server timeouts still apply.
Continue and detach lets the request finish without further pauses. If stopping leaves the script unavailable, choose Retry applied script.

sections.title: Test in the sandbox
paragraphs: Single callback runs only the selected handler, starting with empty state. It bypasses the request and body filters. Use it to check a callback’s returned changes.

Exchange scenario tests filters, request/response callbacks, and carried state together. A pass means no script or processing errors. Inspect which callbacks ran and the final messages to confirm your changes. A simulated upstream failure can still pass.

Neither mode sends traffic or enables the script. Tests use the draft’s capabilities and parameters, but do not verify network behavior or resolve saved response assets. Supply decoded body fixtures without Content-Encoding. Confirm the result with matching proxy traffic.

sections.title: Complete examples
paragraphs: Start with the disabled examples below, or copy a smaller example. Set its filters and capabilities before enabling it; changing source does not grant permissions.

examples.title: Explore the API without changing traffic
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. All switches start false. Enable one switch and its listed capabilities to try a change. For timing, enable shouldRememberRequest and shouldAnnotate, then run an Exchange scenario.

examples.title: Body helpers: text, JSON, forms and raw bytes
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Enable Read bounded bodies. Request body media types: text/plain, application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Response body media types: text/plain, application/json. Body callbacks buffer matching messages even with all switches off. Each replacement lists its required capabilities in the comments.

examples.title: Rewrite a header
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Writable headers: user-agent.

examples.title: Transform a JSON response
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Response body media types: application/json. Enable Read bounded bodies and Replace bodies. Writable headers: content-type.

examples.title: Return a local response
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Path-prefix filter: /fixture. Enable Return responses or select assets.

examples.title: Correlate a request and its completion
examples.settings: Host filter: example.test. Enable Add saved traffic annotations. Test with Exchange scenario or matching proxy traffic.
